name: Columbus Global ruleset
description: Contains Columbus Global rules that are forced during pipeline validation

rules.justification: Spacing around binary operators is enforced by code formatter. Hidden to avoid redundant warnings during development while formatter handles this automatically.
Spacing rules are handled by automatic code formatting. Hidden to reduce noise in diagnostics while maintaining consistent formatting through tooling.
NOT operator spacing is enforced by formatter. Hidden as this is a stylistic concern automatically handled by development tools.
BEGIN..END should only enclose compound statements to maintain code readability and prevent confusion. Error level ensures developers don't add unnecessary code blocks.
Parentheses on function calls ensure consistency and clarity even for parameterless functions. Error level enforces this standard across all code.
BEGIN placement after control structures is a formatting concern handled by code formatter. Hidden to avoid duplicate warnings.
Statement positioning is controlled by automatic formatting. Hidden as formatter ensures consistent code structure.
Variable ordering by type improves readability but is not critical to functionality. Info level suggests best practice without blocking builds.
CASE statements can improve readability over IF-THEN-ELSE but context matters. Info level allows developers to make judgment calls.
Nested WITH statements significantly reduce code readability and make debugging difficult. Error level prevents this anti-pattern.
Cross-application permissions in extensions can cause dependency issues. Warning allows awareness while permitting justified exceptions.
Including permission sets from other applications creates tight coupling. Warning ensures developers consider implications.
Indirect cross-application permissions through permission sets can create hidden dependencies. Warning promotes careful review.
Wildcard permissions in extensions are overly permissive and pose security risks. Warning encourages explicit permission definitions.
Type suffixing improves clarity but modern IDEs provide type information. Hidden as this is a style preference.
Temp prefix for temporary variables is critical to avoid database operation mistakes. Error level prevents potential data integrity issues.
Standard suffixes for TextConst and Label ensure translation consistency and resource management. Error level enforces naming conventions.
Lowering permissions outside tests is usually unintended and potentially dangerous. Info level raises awareness of this practice.
